new_items.statement: Let δ>0. Is it true that, for all sufficiently large n, every K_5-free graph on n vertices with at least δn² edges contains a set of ≫_δ n vertices spanning no triangle? Equivalently, is the Ramsey–Turán density lim_{ε→0} lim_n RT_3(n, K_5, εn)/n² equal to 0?
new_items.label: PRIOR
new_items.prior_work: Balogh and Lenz (2013), 'On the Ramsey–Turán numbers of graphs and hypergraphs', Israel J. Math. 194, 45–68 (shows the density is positive); Liu, Reiher, Sharifzadeh and Staden (2021), 'Geometric constructions for Ramsey–Turán theory' (value is exactly 1/12).
new_items.note: Wiki 2(a): GPT (26 Jan 2026) found the full solution in the literature. Answer: no.

new_items.statement: For k ≥ 2, is the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex graph containing neither a cycle of length 2k−1 nor one of length 2k equal to (1+o(1))(n/2)^{1+1/k}?
new_items.label: PRIOR
new_items.prior_work: Lazebnik, Ustimenko and Woldar (1994), 'Properties of certain families of 2k-cycle-free graphs', J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 60, 293–298 (disproof for k=3,5); Füredi, Naor and Verstraëte (2006), 'On the Turán number for the hexagon', Adv. Math. 203 (alternative disproof for k=3).
new_items.note: Wiki 2(a): GPT-5.4 Pro (28 Mar 2026) found the full solution in the literature. Answer: no.

new_items.statement: Let α be the ordinal ω^{ω²}. In every red/blue colouring of the edges of the complete graph on α, must there be either a red complete subgraph of order type α or a blue triangle (i.e. does α → (α,3)² hold)?
new_items.label: PRIOR
new_items.prior_work: Schipperus (2010), 'Countable partition ordinals', Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 161, 1195–1215; independently Darby.
new_items.note: Wiki 2(a): ChatGPT Deep Research (17 Jan 2026) and Aletheia (1 Feb 2026) found the full solution in the literature. Answer: yes.

new_items.statement: For every 2-colouring of the real numbers, must there exist a set A ⊆ ℝ of cardinality ℵ_1 such that all sums a+b with a ≠ b in A have the same colour?
new_items.label: PRIOR
new_items.prior_work: Komjáth (2016), 'A certain 2-coloring of the reals', Real Anal. Exchange 41(1) (ZFC disproof); independently Soukup and Weiss; under CH: Hindman, Leader and Strauss (2017), 'Pairwise sums in colourings of the reals', Abh. Math. Semin. Univ. Hambg.
new_items.note: Wiki 2(a): GPT (2 Jan 2026) found the full solution in the literature. Answer: no.

new_items.statement: Let x_1 < x_2 < ... be any increasing sequence of integers. Is it true that for almost every α ∈ [0,1] the discrepancy D(N) = max_I |#{n ≤ N : {αx_n} ∈ I} − |I|N| satisfies D(N) ≪ N^{1/2}(log N)^{o(1)}?
new_items.label: PRIOR
new_items.prior_work: Berkes and Philipp (1994), 'The size of trigonometric and Walsh series and uniform distribution mod 1', J. London Math. Soc. (2) 50, 454–464 (sequence with limsup D(N)/(N log N)^{1/2} > 0 a.e.).
new_items.note: Wiki 2(a): Aletheia (1 Feb 2026) found the full solution in the literature. Answer: no.

new_items.statement: Let 1 = d_1 < ... < d_τ(n) = n be the divisors of n and, for α > 1, h_α(n) = Σ_i (d_{i+1}/d_i − 1)^α. Is liminf_{n→∞} h_α(n) bounded by a constant depending only on α?
new_items.label: PRIOR
new_items.prior_work: Vose (1984), 'Integers with consecutive divisors in small ratio', J. Number Theory 19.
new_items.note: Wiki 2(a): ChatGPT Deep Research / Gemini (19 Oct 2025) found the full solution in the literature. Answer: yes.

new_items.statement: For nodes x_1,...,x_n in [−1,1] with Lagrange basis polynomials l_k, set x_0 = −1, x_{n+1} = 1 and Υ = min_{0≤i≤n} max_{x∈[x_i,x_{i+1}]} Σ_k |l_k(x)|. Is Υ ≪ log n, and which node sets maximise Υ (are they characterised by all the interval maxima being equal)?
new_items.label: PRIOR
new_items.prior_work: de Boor and Pinkus (1978), 'Proof of the conjectures of Bernstein and Erdős concerning the optimal nodes for polynomial interpolation', J. Approx. Theory 24, 289–303.
new_items.note: Wiki 2(a): GPT-5.2 Pro (17 Jan 2026) found the full solution in the literature. Shares its source with key item 1129, so the two are not independent.

new_items.statement: Let α > 0 be irrational. Is the set of n ≥ 1 with ‖αn²‖ < 1/log n (distance to the nearest integer) an additive basis of order 2?
new_items.label: PRIOR
new_items.prior_work: Konieczny (2016), 'Sets of recurrence as bases for the positive integers', Acta Arith. 174(4) (disproof for a.e. α and α = √2). Title matched by search; the site cites it only as [Ko16b].
new_items.note: Wiki 2(a): GPT-5.2 Thinking (26 Jan 2026) found the full solution in the literature. Answer: no.

new_items.statement: Let f_k(n) be the number of elements of order k in the symmetric group S_n. For which k is f_k(n) maximal, and how large is the maximum?
new_items.label: PRIOR
new_items.prior_work: Beker (2025), 'The most probable order of a random permutation', arXiv:2510.11698 (max_k f_k(n) ~ (n−1)!, with the maximising k characterised).
new_items.note: Wiki 2(a): GPT-5.2 Thinking (24 Jan 2026) found the full solution in the literature (a 2025 preprint).

new_items.statement: Let f_r(n) be maximal such that any graph G in which every m-vertex subgraph is the union of a graph of chromatic number ≤ r and a graph with ≤ f_r(m) edges has chromatic number ≤ r+1. Is f_2(n) ≫ n, and more generally f_r(n) ≫_r n?
new_items.label: PRIOR
new_items.prior_work: Rödl (1982), 'Nearly bipartite graphs with large chromatic number', Combinatorica 2, 377–383 (implies f_r(n) = o(n)).
new_items.note: Wiki 1(d): Chojecki + GPT-5.5 Pro listed as a full solution (28 Apr 2026). The site page resolves it via Rödl's 1982 construction, which Tang pointed out in the comments. Answer: no. Moderate confidence: the wiki has not moved it to 1(b).

new_items.statement: Let S ⊂ ℝ be a set of infinite Lebesgue measure such that x/y is never an integer for distinct x, y ∈ S. How fast can |S ∩ (0,x)| tend to infinity?
new_items.label: NEW
new_items.note: Wiki 1(d): Ho + GPT-5.4 Pro full solution (19 Apr 2026). Such S with |S∩(0,x)| ≥ F(x) exists iff ∫_1^∞ F(x)/x² dx < ∞. Prior work (Haight 1970, Szemerédi 1971) covered existence only.

new_items.statement: Let A ⊆ {1,...,N} contain no solution to at = b with a, b ∈ A where the smallest prime factor of t exceeds a. Estimate the maximum of (1/log N) Σ_{n∈A} 1/n.
new_items.label: NEW
new_items.note: Wiki 1(d): Chojecki + GPT-5.4 Pro full solution (15 Apr 2026): max = (c+o(1)) log N with explicit c ≈ 0.618. Earlier results only o(log N) or Behrend-type.

new_items.statement: Let h(n) be the longest chain of primes p_1 < ... < p_ℓ dividing n with p_{i+1} ≡ 1 mod p_i, and H(n) the longest chain of divisors d_1 < ... < d_u of n with d_{i+1} ≡ 1 mod d_i. Estimate h(n) and H(n); is H(n)/h(n) → ∞ for almost all n?
new_items.label: NEW
new_items.note: Wiki 1(d): Mallen, Turturean + GPT-5.5 Pro / Claude / Aristotle full solution (Lean, Apr–Jun 2026): log_* n ≪ h(n) ≤ H(n) ≪ log_* n for almost all n, so the answer is no. Page cites no prior solution.

new_items.statement: For A, B ⊆ {1,...,N}, let F(A,B) be the number of integers m having exactly one representation m = ab with a ∈ A, b ∈ B. Estimate the maximum of F(A,B).
new_items.label: NEW
new_items.note: Wiki 1(d): Chojecki + GPT-5.5 Pro full solution (26 Apr 2026): max ≍ N²/((log N)^δ (log log N)^{3/2}), δ = 1 − (1+log log 2)/log 2. The upper bound is immediate from Ford (2008); the AI proved the lower bound using Ford-type estimates. The answer itself was not previously stated.

new_items.statement: Let a_1, a_2, ... be positive integers with a_n → ∞. Is Σ_n τ(n)/(a_1 a_2 ⋯ a_n) irrational, where τ(n) is the number of divisors of n?
new_items.label: NEW
new_items.note: Wiki 1(c): GPT-5.4 Pro full solution (14 Apr 2026), building on Tao–Teräväinen (2025); the page credits Chojecki + GPT-5.4 Pro (Lean). Prior: only the monotone case (Erdős–Straus) and constant a_n.

new_items.statement: Let C > 0. Are there infinitely many integers a, b, n with a + b > n + C log n such that the denominator of n!/(a! b!) contains only primes bounded in terms of C?
new_items.label: NEW
new_items.note: Wiki 1(c): Aristotle + GPT-5.2 Pro full solution (Lean, 8–10 Jan 2026), adapting the AI solution of a sibling problem. Page: Barreto/Leeham with ChatGPT+Aristotle, no prior literature.

new_items.statement: For nodes x_1,...,x_n in [−1,1] with Lagrange basis polynomials l_k, let λ(x) = Σ_k |l_k(x)|. Is it true that for every fixed −1 ≤ a < b ≤ 1, max_{x∈[a,b]} λ(x) > (2/π − o(1)) log n?
new_items.label: NEW
new_items.note: Wiki 1(d): Bhalla, Sothanaphan, Tao with AlphaEvolve/Claude/Gemini/GPT full solution (Feb–Mar 2026); page credits Tao [Ta26b] with the bound (2/π) log n − O(1). Prior: full interval only (Bernstein 1931, Erdős 1961) and ≫ log n on subintervals (Erdős–Szabados 1978).

new_items.statement: Let E ⊂ (0,∞) have positive measure. Is it true that for almost every x > 0 and all sufficiently large integers n there is an integer r ≥ 1 with nx ∈ r·E?
new_items.label: NEW
new_items.note: Wiki 1(c): Aristotle + Claude Opus 4.7 + GPT-5.4 Pro full solution (Lean, Apr–Jun 2026), building on Buczolich–Mauldin (1999). Page: counterexample by ebarschkis via a variant of the Buczolich–Mauldin construction. Answer: no.
